migration_behavior.observation: The repository currently carries a squashed baseline only. Every candidate column is present in the baseline/snapshot. A cleanup against already-created databases cannot be represented safely by editing only 0000; it needs the repository's approved forward-migration/rebaseline procedure. FK/index/CHECK dependent columns require dependent DDL changes in the same migration.
migration_behavior.warning: No schema or migration edit was made during the candidate matrix.

tool_findings: Raw SQL is only annotated raw? and is not attributed to a table, producing false read-only verdicts for all three plugin_kv identity/scope columns.
INSERT ... SELECT projections are not recognized as writes, producing false read-only verdicts for refinery_schemas id/owner_id/created_at and embed_space_state owner_id/scope.
Whole-row arrays/spreads are conservatively opaque, which is safe for provider_rows and theme_clusters writes but cannot distinguish actual per-column writes.

DDL consumers (PK/unique partial index/FK action/CHECK/index expression) are not sufficient to prevent write-only candidates; origin fields, distributed_by, and is_primary prove that an application read is not required for a column to be load-bearing.

The row-shape read arm materially overcounts homonyms: imagery provider/connectionId, session connectionId/createdAt, and chat_stream_events id/createdAt receive unrelated reads. The safe overcount hides never-populated columns, so triage must still compare actual table-qualified access and writers.
Default-provenance suppression can be defeated by homonym row-shape reads, as session_entries.created_at demonstrates.
